source: SPOT figure 1's sampler model (benchmarks/spot_figures/figure1.py at the spotfig branch's head, its cards) with one replay block per layer of a token: for each scope, budget and proof overhead, the least number K of incorrect proof blocks the plan detects with probability at least 1 - delta, times a proof block's output bits, the plan's statement fill at its k; GLM-5.3's sizes from its pinned config (zai-org/GLM-5.3@aca966e4e02791568aa6a4ced368624b3d897f42 config.json sha256 3ac72612095574542f7fff847ada8e59d9199dd8af44bdf625d7e02615572e69). It is the quantity infiltration_bound reads off an integrity profile, computed here from the model, not by the consumer; provisional until the consumer is on main and figure1 computes it.

value.caption: Deferred interiors at a layer of a token (solid): serving commits each layer's residual stream, MLA K/V and indexer keys (1.05 MB a token, hashed at 2.1% of the scope's compute, outside the budget); a replay block is one layer of one token (its footprint at most 6,691 proof blocks), and a statement holds one replay block's sampled proof blocks of one Definition. The bound is the write form (infiltration_bound): the output bits of the incorrect proof blocks, the committed values the prover wrote in place of what the circuit computes, served or not, so no output size caps it. One steering vector (one token, one layer) is 98,304 bits. This is not the exfiltration panel's design: two-stage there commits only tokens and certifies infiltration only through the served outputs, and under this design exfiltration is at most this curve plus which blocks are wrong. Advice is not a write, so the curves hold in every advice regime.
